answer: Each identity links to a network whose BGP announcements have a stable history: the prefix must have been announced consistently by the same origin AS for months. A copper cable laid once and left alone tells a story; a prefix that appears, vanishes, and reappears under different origins tells another. The ferrous backbone of the internet remembers every announcement, and the network checks that history before trusting an identity. A jetty built on shifting sand collapses: a farm renting short-lived prefixes cannot show the steady record that honest operators accumulate.
